lukas.novak@mail.example | +358 00 000 0003 | Tampere, Finland

Education

Experience

Signal Processing Engineer
Tuulikallio Embedded Systems, Tampere
Sep 2017 – Aug 2019, Jan 2021 – present

- Design and implement real-time beamforming algorithms in C targeting TI C6000 DSP processors for the company’s multi-channel acoustic sensor product line; responsible for the full signal chain from ADC input through spatial filtering to detection output
- Build and maintain the production Python test and validation infrastructure (pytest, Jenkins CI) used across Tuulikallio’s sensor products, including automated regression testing, waveform generation, and performance benchmarking with hardware-in-the-loop rigs
- Apply my graduate research in wave physics and array theory from the Sakura National University to the design of narrowband and wideband beamformers; the mathematical framework from my MSc thesis on acoustic wavefield decomposition still underpins most of the spatial filtering work I do

Aug 2019 – Dec 2020: Career break (redundancy during company restructuring; spent the period requalifying through intensive short courses in FPGA design and embedded real-time systems)

Selected Projects

Satellite Payload Beamformer Prototype (Tuulikallio, 2022–2023)
Developed a 16-element digital beamforming prototype for a customer’s LEO satellite communications payload. Designed the steering and calibration firmware running on a Xilinx Zynq SoC. Extensive simulation of beam patterns under spacecraft attitude uncertainty. This was an EORA-subcontracted project requiring EU work authorisation; I hold a Finnish permanent residence permit (A-permit, continuous).

Oulu Field Trial (Tuulikallio, 2024)
Deployed and tested a 32-channel phased array prototype at a customer site in Oulu for three months. Lived in Oulu during the trial and worked on-site with the end customer’s systems integration team. Open to relocating permanently — I found the city and its engineering community genuinely appealing.

Skills & Tools

- Array signal processing: delay-and-sum, MVDR, adaptive nulling, wideband beamforming
- C/C++ (bare-metal and RTOS), Python (NumPy, SciPy, pytest), MATLAB/Simulink
- DSP platforms: TI C6000 multicore, Xilinx Zynq
- Co-author: “Wideband beamforming for LEO payload applications,” Proc. BALSIPCO, 2023
- Open-source: github.example/example-lnovak — Python array processing toolkit (~120 stars)
- Languages: Czech (native), English (fluent — all professional work conducted in English since 2016), Finnish (intermediate / B1), Japanese (conversational)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
I spent three months living in Oulu last year for a field deployment, and by the end of it I was browsing rental listings. The city’s engineering community is smaller than Tampere’s or Helsinki’s but remarkably concentrated in RF and photonics — you run into the same people at Suvanto seminars and local industry events, which keeps collaboration straightforward and keeps everyone honest about the quality of their work. When I saw the Senior Signal Processing Engineer posting at Kaikuvaara, it felt like the right reason to make a permanent move.

My background is in array signal processing and embedded real-time implementation. I have been at Tuulikallio Embedded Systems since 2017, with a break in 2019–2020 after a round of redundancies during a company restructuring. That period was frustrating — I spent most of it requalifying through intensive short courses in FPGA design and real-time embedded systems, which in hindsight made me a considerably better engineer even though I would not recommend the circumstances. Since coming back in January 2021, my work has focused on digital beamforming for multi-channel sensor systems, including a satellite payload beamformer prototype that went through a full EORA subcontract review. That project was the most technically demanding I have worked on: sixteen elements, real-time calibration under hard power and latency constraints, and trade-offs at every design level.

The aspects of the Kaikuvaara role that stand out to me are the combination of algorithm development and close-to-hardware implementation. At Tuulikallio I spend roughly equal time writing beamforming algorithms in C for DSP processors and building the Python infrastructure to test and validate them, and I do my strongest work when I can move between those two levels rather than being confined to one. My MSc at the Sakura National University was in applied physics — wave propagation and array theory — and that analytical grounding still shapes how I approach new problems even when the application domain shifts. The constrained optimisation methods and statistical estimation framework I learned there are tools I reach for constantly.

I should also mention that I am comfortable with estimation-theoretic methods including Kalman filtering, which I understand may be relevant to some of Kaikuvaara’s tracking and calibration work.

What I can offer concretely: nine years building real-time spatial filtering systems, familiarity with the full path from simulation through embedded deployment, and a genuine desire to be in Oulu. I already know engineers in the local community from my time at the field trial, and I value the kind of place where people from different organisations actually talk to each other.

Available at your convenience.

Lukas Novak

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
